utterances.text: I have, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the department of civil affairs in the 1st Corps of the Krajina did indeed have the task which are indicated in this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The civilian affairs organs had precisely the tasks that are reflected in bullet point 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the 1st Corps of the Krajina receive the Main Staff orders concerning the passage of convoys?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Corps received instructions from the Main Staff for the passage of certain convoys through the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps. This was done down the chain of command from the Main Staff to the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the area of the 1st Krajina Corps were there convoys which went through?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were UNPROFOR convoys, there were UNHCR convoys, and there were also the International Committee of the Red Cross convoy. They all came from Zagreb, went through Gradiska, Banja Luka, and further on towards Zenica or Tesanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D782. This is an order from the Main Staff of the 1st August, 1993. As you may see, this order was sent also to the 1st Krajina Corps. And could the witness be shown page 2, first paragraph on page 2. It's also the first paragraph of page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said that you received instructions, orders, from the Main Staff. Did you receive authorisations concerning certain -- the convoys, specific convoys?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, we received orders which provided the details of the type of convoy, its route, and what the convoy contained, what kind of goods. This applied to UNPROFOR convoys.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Indeed, if you -- if we could come back to the first page of the order. You can see that this order concerns the movements of UNPROFOR. Can you see this at the top of the document, the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Yes. That's a document about the movement of the UNPROFOR through the territory of Republika Srpska received from the command of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In 1993, could convoys pass without the authorisation of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There were certain attempts by convoys to pass, but we always reported to the Main Staff about such attempts and requested their opinion and orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were there orders concerning precisely a ban of passage without an authorisation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There were such orders, Your Honours, but I can't recall exactly when at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D774. This is an order from the Main Staff of 15 May 1993. It is sent to all the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'm interested particularly in this order, the one but last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honour, honouring this order of the 15th of March, 1993, not a single convoy could pass through the area of the 1st Krajina Corps without prior authorisation and announcement in keeping with the orders of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown a notification of the passage of convoy of the army of the Republika Srpska. This is a notification sent to the Drina Corps. It is 5D839.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So this is a notification sent to the Drina Corps and Sarajevo Corps. Did this notification received by the 1st Krajina Corps look like this one?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The notification received by the 1st Krajina Corps, in terms of substance and format, was similar. Of course the names were different, and there were different vehicles and cargo, but the order of items is identical.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this note, notification, on 16 August 1994, one sees a detailed specification of the goods carried. For instance, five kilos of sugar, 10 litres of milk, 40 yogurts and so on. Forty containers. What was the case for the 1st Krajina Corps? Should foodstuffs be specified in such detail?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The goods were always specified.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said that there had been some attempts for convoys to try and pass without authorisation. Have you ever seen an order from the Main Staff demanding that illegal passages should be stop or prohibited?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Yes, there was such an order passed on down to some units, the units that manned the check-points. Our situation was peculiar, because convoys entered from Republic of Croatia crossing a bridge, so it was not possible to enter without authorisation south of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D815. This is a document from the Main Staff. I think the date is 30 January 1994. This document is sent to the 2nd Krajina Corps and to Eastern Bosnia Corps and to the Sarajevo Corps. As for the 1st Krajina Corps and the Drina Corps and the Hercegovina Corps, they have received this document only for information, for their information.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at this document and tell us why the 1st Krajina Corps receives this document for information only?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: We received this document for our information, because the Main Staff of the VRS had knowledge of such illegal actions, and the idea was that adequate steps be taken into the area covered by the 1st Corps to prevent such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: A while ago we were speaking of the UNPROFOR convoys. Were there any specific orders concerning the convoys of humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There had been requests by the UNPROFOR that they be allowed to escort UNHCR convoys, that their observers or other personnel escort these convoys through the area of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We saw a while ago an order from the Main Staff concerning the UNPROFOR convoys. Did the 1st Krajina Corps receive other orders concerning the passage of international organisations? I specify: Humanitarian international organisations.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Main Staff very frequently issued instructions regarding both the UNPROFOR and international humanitarian organisations. Everything that was received by the other corps was also received in the form of an order or information by the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1285 [as interpreted]. This is an order of the 1st of August, 1993, from the Main Staff, sent to all the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: As you may see, this is an order concerning the movement of humanitarian aid, and the date is 1st August 1993, precisely the same date as the order which we saw a moment ago and which concerned the passage of the UNPROFOR convoys. And for the transcript it was 5D782. Can you explain why the Main Staff, on the same day, issued two orders, one for the passage of UNPROFOR and the other one for the passage of humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: These two activities are a bit different. UNPROFOR convoys meant armed convoys, armed to a smaller or lesser extent. And there was an UNPROFOR office at Pale, and in order to abbreviate the procedure it was placed in the hands of the army so that the army negotiates directly with the UNPROFOR the passage of their convoys; whereas humanitarian convoys in this period were regulated, as dated here, through the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'm going to stray away from the period when you were at the Main Staff towards the end of 1994 and beginning the 1995. When you were at the Main Staff, do you know who was in charge of giving authorisations for the passage of humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: A coordinating body was formed and attached to the Government of Republika Srpska. It was based in Pale, and it issued approvals for the passage of humanitarian convoys and notified them, in fact, to the Main Staff of the VRS in order to trigger further procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about this organ, the coordination organ? When was it established?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I cannot give you an exact answer to that question. I know that a member of that body from the Main Staff of the VRS was Colonel Milos Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness 5D806.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is an order dated 30th of December, 1993, coming from the Main Staff. The coordinating organ is mentioned in the first paragraph. I would like to examine page 2 in English and page 2 in B/C/S, item 7. At item 7 you can read the following: "[In English] This order shall come into force on 1 January 1994 and be amended on receipt of the document from the Coordinating Body for Humanitarian Aid which describes the new system of humanitarian aid in detail." [Interpretation] Does this refresh your memory, and can you recall anything about the period in time when this coordinating organ was established?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Obviously it was established earlier. I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this might be a convenient moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, in 1993, 1994, were the convoys being checked?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: They were always checked, at the entrance check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was it possible for a convoy to go through without being inspected at that time, 1993, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was impossible for a convoy to pass without being inspected.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were there any specific orders for check-points and the staff and officers who inspected these convoys?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, there was an order issued by the Main Staff which regulated the appearance of the check-point where convoys were inspected. It was also stipulated that appropriate manpower and equipment be selected for the task and that full attention be paid to civilised behaviour and civilised treatment of the internationals involved in the transportation regardless of their origin, whether they were UNPROFOR or any other international organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'd like to show you 5D771. This is an order from the Main Staff sent to all the corps, and it deals with UNPROFOR convoys and humanitarian aid convoys of the 9th of April, 1993. Please look at item 1.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the 1st Krajina Corps take any specific measures to abide by this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, pursuant to this order which reached the assistant commander for civilian affairs, the assistant commander compiled another document which the commander signed and which was sent to the unit that was in charge of the inspection of convoys. The assistant commander for civilian affairs, i.e., his liaison officer, in the specific case it was me, we were duty-bound to check the implementation of that order on the ground. We had to perform regular checks of the implementation of the order. The brigade wherein whose area of responsibility the check-point was included the activities of that check-point into its regular daily reports and mentioned any convoys that would pass through.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the Main Staff then send other orders relating to the quality and intensity of convoy checks?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There were such orders. MS. FAUVEAU [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness 5D802.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is another order relating to the inspections of convoy, in this specific instance humanitarian aid convoys. Please examine item 2. It's to be found at the very bottom of page 1. And this order is dated 24th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I've looked at item 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Why was it necessary to reissue a similar order six or seven months later?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: As I have already said it, the corps commands analysed the work of the check-point, and they informed the Main Staff about any problems. In a desire to avoid any conflicts and to enable a smooth passage of convoys, the Main Staff re-emphasised that issue. I suppose that there may have been minor problems at some of the check-points, and the one in the 1st Krajina Corps was not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Earlier at page 52, line 22, you mentioned the way check-points were organised. I'd like to show you 5D789. This is an order dated 30th of August, 1993, and it was sent to all the corps of the VRS. Look at item 2. It indicates clearly that check-points must be organised in an adequate way, but what is -- what I am more interested in is item 1, which states that: "Check-points must function continuously, 24 hours a day." Does the fact that check-points were operational 24 hours a day pose a number of problems in terms of safety, or did it pose such problems?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There were problems. There were security issues. Working during the day is not the same as working during the night. Very often there were no lights. The place was not lit or, rather, lights had to be improvised in such places. And the intention behind this order was to allow UNPROFOR forces and peacekeeping organisations to be able to pass smoothly around the clock. At one point there were a lot of convoys, and it was difficult for all of them to be let through during the day. Some of them had to wait for nightfall to pass, and this order provided for such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you received, very shortly afterwards, another order relating to movements after nightfall?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I can't remember, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Let's turn now to 5D790. This is an order from the Main Staff dated 6th of September, 1993, and sent to all corps. Please look at the first paragraph of this order.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Yes, I've had a look at the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you now remember this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, we were mentioning checks. Why were these checks and inspections compulsory? I mean, inspecting the convoys.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Well, firstly, this was agreed. This was part of the negotiating procedure with those who were in charge of the transportation of the goods, including UNPROFOR. Checks were needed because most convoys moved on to the territory under the control of the other side. There were cases of materials being transported which were not declared, which might have been of military significance or use for the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What happened -- what happened when someone refused to inspect checks -- convoys? What was the procedure when a convoy refused to let itself be inspected?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the 1st Corps we had a case of that kind. An UNHCR convoy on route from Zagreb and with an intention to proceed towards Travnik would not allow us to check the cargo. They simply had to return to their departure point in Zagreb after a short conversation. I suppose that they must have been transporting something that didn't -- that they did not want the check-points to discover.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the Main Staff inform you of the procedure of -- that was to be applied whenever such incidents occurred at check-points?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There was also a procedure envisaged for cases when goods on the list are found. In that case such goods would be seized, kept, and the Main Staff would be notified.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Let's now turn to 5D809. This is an order from the Main Staff dated 16th of January, 1994. It was sent to all corps. I would like to look at item 2 of this order. It's on page 1 both in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I have looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'd like to know specifically whether we're talking about convoys here or any missions conducted by the international organisations located in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: In this item 2 reference is made specifically to the UNPROFOR but also other international organisations. Minor problems were to be resolved on the spot, that is at brigade or corps level, things that could be handled, whereas more complex problems would have to be reported as soon as possible to the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When there were incidents or difficulties in the 1st Krajina Corps in 1993 and 1994, who would you turn to at the Main Staff to inform them? Who was your contact point?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: In technical professional terms, we approached Colonel Magazin, who was in charge of all convoy relate issues at the Main Staff. Of course another notification would go to the operation's officer on duty or the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you said about the operations officer on duty, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The duty operations officer had the communication line towards the command, and in the sector for civilian affairs, there was also a civilian telephone; and if an opinion was needed urgently we could use that line because it was quicker. We had secure communications on both sides, but of course the first request would be addressed to the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you were serving in the 1st Krajina Corps did you have any information relating to the activities of international humanitarian organisations and/or UNPROFOR which would have been contrary to their mission?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Yes, we had such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could we now move on to 5D817. This is an order from the Main Staff dated 12th of February, 1994. It was sent to all corps. The preamble of the order relates to organisations -- to activities planned and organised by UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations related to supplying and providing the Muslims with military equipment. Did you ever get such information?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honour, we did receive information of this kind, and we took the appropriate steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Let's now move on to 5D818. In the Krajina Corps, did you conduct an analysis of passage of the convoys and of the goods? Just so you know, this is a report from the Drina Corps. The only thing I'm interested in here is whether you in the 1st Krajina Corps drafted similar reports and information notes.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: An analysis would be done and periodic reports would be made to the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you receive any information according to which certain humanitarian organisations had activities of intelligence, were involved in intelligence activities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honour, we did have intelligence that certain humanitarian organisations under the cloak of providing humanitarian aid are engaged in intelligence work and consequently our checks became more meticulous.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown two small documents on which I wish to ask a question. The first is 5D781. And this is a notification of the Main Staff sent to the Drina Corps on the 29th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please have a look at the second paragraph which has to do with the activities of the HCR, UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown the same type document, 5D780, which was sent to the Drina Corps and to the Sarajevo Corps, dated 27 July 1993, which is approximately the same period.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: As you may see in the last paragraph it's practically identical to the paragraph you read beforehand in the former document.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to what you remember, do you recall any period during which this sort of information were specifically -- were quite frequently received?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The reports were more frequent in July and August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember whether according -- at the same period or maybe a bit later the Krajina Corps received a document from the Main Staff indicating indeed that there were intelligence activities within humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I remember documents like that as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D796.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is a document from the Main Staff, dated 26 September 1993. It was sent to all corps. In the second paragraph you see that the intelligence activities of UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations have intensified recently.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This type of information, did it have an influence on the type of checks on convoys?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: We intensified activities aimed at detecting video equipment and communications equipment either announced or unannounced, and we would make a brief evaluation of all the purposes that such equipment could be used for.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown on this first page a bit lower. In English it's also on the first page, third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see in this document that there's video camera recording which is mentioned. These goods, video cameras and photo cameras, were they authorised? Were these goods transported in the humanitarian convoys?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: That item was not authorised, but there had been attempts to smuggle in that sort of equipment, especially when smaller patrols or groups had been announced on routes leading to protected areas. In the zone of the 1st Corps, we had very good cooperation with civilian police who were involved in monitoring the passage of convoys but also individuals, and that avoided us unnecessary delays that would have hindered the passage of convoys, groups of vehicles, or individual vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D794.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is a report from the Drina Corps sent to Colonel Magazin, which you mentioned a while ago, and at the -- in the second paragraph in the middle, you can see that the convoy was transporting video cameras, photo cameras, films, radios, and so on. Could you explain why the video equipment and photo cameras were not authorised in particular?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honour, this equipment could have been used, and there are reports that it was indeed used, for filming the positions of our units in the area through which they passed and that the information obtained in this way was made available to the enemy side. They often explained that it was for their own use, even their own private use, as a memento of their mission. Of course we couldn't accept that in view of the routes along which they passed, so we seized, confiscate such equipment and sometimes returned it to them when they -- on their way back.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Before we stop, you were a JNA officer before the war. What was the JNA position towards the question of recording video clips and photographs of these buildings or vehicles? What was the position of the JNA about this equipment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: This is not quite clear. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I will repeat. Did the JNA authorise its buildings and its equipment, its vehicles, or any other sort of equipment during peacetime before the war could be filmed or recorded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The rules made clear what must not be filmed or photographed. Such notices were placed on installations and on the roads. It was indicated on which stretch of the road, if it was a military training ground or something like that was not to be filmed or photographed. Not every facility, not every installation could be captured on camera.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kralj, what was your --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- shall we break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In 1993 to 1995? What was your rank. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in 1993 I was a major in the armoured mechanised units until mid-1995 when I was promoted into lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn for today and resume at 9.00 tomorrow, during which time you're not supposed to talk to anybody or discuss your evidence with anybody. Do you understand, Mr. Kralj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand my role as a witness completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
